SLOT-MATH VERIFICATION (my method, independently recomputed): CH8_L1_MIN_SLOT_SECONDS = 4.5 confirmed — L1 is 94 chars x 34 ms = 3.20 s reveal + 1.3 s read. CH8_L2_MIN_SLOT_SECONDS = 3.0 confirmed — L2 is 65 chars (Chapter's 66 is off by one, immaterial) = 2.21 s reveal + 0.79 s read. L3 is 58 chars = 1.97 s reveal, and the measured movie-pace gap from the surface-to-descent phase edge to deep_space is ~2.0 s (fine trace: edge by t=7043, deep_space ~9031) — L3 firing at the edge completes its reveal with near-zero margin at movie pace and cannot survive a later t_L2+3.0 firing there. The drop rule is therefore not a compromise but the only honest structure; the paced scripted route is the load-bearing guarantee and its L3 margin must be MEASURED, not assumed (condition C3). The L3-never-interrupts-L2 property is guaranteed by construction (3.0 slot >= 2.21 + 0.79) and must be asserted as such.

RULING (c) — the mid-reveal interruption exception: ACCEPTED, narrowly, as a carve-out in my own law. The no-mid-reveal-overwrite law exists to stop SYSTEM-caused overwrites from stealing authored reading time — the defect class this run kills. A player-caused interruption is different in kind and here it is diegetic: the interrupting event is the player's own committed act, and L2's text IS the self-order — the act interrupting the thought enacts the line ('hold it.' arriving as the thumb commits). Conditions on the carve-out: (1) bounded to exactly the L1-to-L2 pair via the phase-edge acceleration; the timer path (t_L1 + 4.5) must never interrupt — by construction it cannot (4.5 >= 3.20 + 1.3), and tests must assert player-caused-only; (2) the exception must not cascade — L3 never interrupts L2 mid-reveal, asserted via the 3.0 s constant; (3) the contract records it as THE SINGLE authored exception, non-precedential: any future exception to the no-mid-reveal law requires full triad signature; (4) the interruption must be imaged (capture Route B below) so reviewers score it as authored, not as a slot collision.
